evidence.quote: allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events
Australia’s Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral reef in the world

criteria.reasoning: Clear Australian benefit, users named, function described with bleaching statistics and literature links. No formal goals, objectives or quantified requirements for orbit, revisit, resolution or latency.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart

criteria.reasoning: Gantt with weekly tasks and source list provided, feasible sequence. Not tailored to reef payload needs, no contingencies or variation provision, no justification of plan against mission concept.
No calculations, orbit parameters, simulations or payload analysis shown. Only background reading and generic STK tutorials claimed, which is not mission-specific technical progress.

evidence.quote: The final report is due on 20/11/20 at 5pm

criteria.reasoning: Readable with headings and generally clear writing. Figure has no number or caption, formatting inconsistent, references are bare URLs and Useful Links not matched to in-text citations.

technical_issues.issue: No quantified mission requirements for spatial/spectral resolution, revisit, coverage of 344400 km2 reef, or latency for near-real-time; water-penetration and atmospheric constraints of colour-based bleaching detection not addressed.
No launch, orbit, COE, communications or deorbit calculations or STK outputs; term AOEs is non-standard and undefined; tutorials do not demonstrate design progress.

overall: Good reef-monitoring rationale with users and sources, workable schedule using STK. Lacks quantified requirements and any real technical results to guide full design.
